Estimate a quadratic mean diameter from dominant height

Source: R/synthetic_inventory.R
estimate_dq_from_hdom.Rd

Applies a species-specific power-law allometry $$D_g \approx a_{species} \cdot H_{dom}^b$$ with \(b = 0.9\) (gently sub-linear). The per-species \(a_{species}\) is calibrated against the mean \((H_0, D_g)\) pair observed in the French National Forest Inventory — i.e. Charru et al. 2012 Table 1 (mean \(D_g\)) crossed with Charru et al. 2017 Table 1 (mean \(H_0\)) for the 8 species covered by both, with extensions using typical IFN H_0 values for PSME, PIPI, PILA, and broadleaf-genus defaults for CASA and POSP.

Usage

estimate_dq_from_hdom(H_dom, species)

Arguments

H_dom

Numeric vector. Dominant height in metres.

species

Character vector of IFN species codes (recycled against H_dom).

Value

Numeric vector of estimated \(D_g\) in cm, clamped to each species' observed range. NA when H_dom is NA, non-positive or below 6 m (stands too young for this allometry).

Details

The relationship is valid only for pure even-aged stands. Multi-layered or strongly irregular stands will still be approximated — the estimate then reflects a biased mean diameter of the dominant social position. The output is clamped to the observed \(D_g\) range of each species (Charru 2012 Table 1) to avoid extrapolation artefacts at very small or very large \(H_{dom}\).

Examples

estimate_dq_from_hdom(H_dom = 25, species = "FASY")
#> [1] 27.59599
estimate_dq_from_hdom(
  H_dom   = c(18, 25, 30),
  species = c("QUPE", "FASY", "PIAB")
)
#> [1] 18.21380 27.59599 35.14301
